articles.title: The last whistle for Thala: MS Dhoni's Chennai story was always bigger than cricket
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: On Babu Jagjeevan Ram Street, a short distance from Chepauk, Mohammad Arif has a shop named Dhoni Sports.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: On Babu Jagjeevan Ram Street, a short distance from Chepauk, Mohammad Arif has a shop named Dhoni Sports. He set it up nearly a decade ago, driven by his admiration for the former India captain. There was one hope behind the name, too: that Dhoni would someday walk through its doors.At Dakshin, the South Indian restaurant at Chennai's Crown Plaza, MD Suresh had a different way of being connected to the cricketer. For years, he prepared the filter coffee Dhoni liked. Chennai Super Kings stayed at the hotel for nearly a decade during their home assignments, and Dhoni enjoyed watching Suresh make the brew.Nabeel VP, originally from Malappuram and now settled in Chennai, found his own place in the city's Dhoni and CSK fan culture. A member of the All Kerala Dhoni Fans Association and connected with the Whistle Podu Army, he was part of groups that organised charity initiatives around Dhoni's birthday.In 2020, he travelled from Shimla to Delhi after learning Dhoni was flying out of the capital, hoping to meet his hero. He waited at the boarding gates with files documenting their work. Dhoni stopped, heard him out, patted his shoulder and said, “Keep up the good work”. He even wanted to keep the file as a memory. For Nabeel, that brief meeting became a moment to cherish.Therein lay something of the Dhoni phenomenon. In Chennai, it was the familiarity of a favourite coffee, the hope of a visit to a neighbourhood shop, the yellow jersey and the whistles that followed him. It was also a fan culture that reached beyond the city, bringing people together through their admiration for one cricketer and one team.For Nabeel, the appeal of Dhoni and CSK was also about the experience of being in the stands. “Movies are for two hours, right? But this happens right in front of us for four hours; four hours of entertainment.”It began, though, with a decision at the inaugural IPL auction in 2008. Chennai Super Kings secured Dhoni for $1.5 million, around Rs 6 crore, making him the most expensive player at the auction. On November 17, 2026, the franchise confirmed that Dhoni had retired as a player and would take up a mentoring role from IPL 2027. His last appearance had come in CSK's final fixture of IPL 2025; he did not play in the 2026 season.Five titles, and the nights that made themThe first glimpse of what Dhoni could mean to Chennai came before CSK had won anything. In 2010, with a place in the playoffs at stake against Kings XI Punjab, he made an unbeaten 54 to take his side home. It was the sort of innings that would become familiar over the next decade and a half: a difficult situation, a finish that seemed to arrive almost on cue, and a captain who rarely gave away what he was thinking.By the end of that season, CSK had their first IPL title. Dhoni's contribution was not always about the runs he scored. In the 2011 final against Royal Challengers Bengaluru, he promoted himself to No. 3 and made 22 off 13 balls as CSK posted 205 before winning by 58 runs. The title defence made them the first team to win consecutive IPL crowns.Then came the two-year suspension, and the sight of Dhoni in a different yellow-less jersey. His return in 2018 was one of the defining chapters of the CSK story. The team was labelled a 'Dad's Army', but Dhoni and his group answered on the field. Against Royal Challengers Bengaluru that season, chasing 206, CSK were 74/4 when he joined Ambati Rayudu. Their 101-run partnership turned the chase around. Dhoni finished unbeaten on 70 off 34 balls, hitting the winning six with two deliveries to spare.There was another reminder of his ability to make a game feel unfinished until the very last ball in Bengaluru the following year. Chasing 162 against RCB, CSK had slipped to 28/4. Dhoni made 84 not out off 48 balls, taking the chase to the final over. With 26 needed, he struck 24 off the first five deliveries - four, six, six, two, six - before CSK fell one run short. It was a defeat, but one that captured the hold he had over a game, and over the people watching him.The late-innings numbers put that reputation into perspective. Dhoni scored 3,468 runs in overs 16 to 20, more than any batter in IPL history between 2008 and 2025. Those runs came at a strike rate of 175, with 208 sixes. In the 20th over alone, he scored 844 runs at a strike rate of 243.2. The next batter on that list, Ravindra Jadeja, has 407.Even as his batting role changed in the later seasons, the capacity for one last intervention remained. In the 2021 Qualifier 1 against Delhi Capitals, CSK lost their way after being 113/1, slipping to 160/6 in the 20th over. Dhoni walked in ahead of Jadeja and made an unbeaten 18 off six balls, hitting three fours and a six to take CSK into the final. It was a small innings by his standards, but a familiar finish.That ability to take a game deep was only one part of his contribution.Behind the stumps, Dhoni's sharp hands and anticipation became as much a part of the CSK identity as his batting. In the 2018 final against Sunrisers Hyderabad, he stumped Kane Williamson for 47. It was a significant moment in the match, and another marker in Dhoni's growing record: he has 47 IPL stumpings, the most by any wicketkeeper in the league. His 201 designated-keeper dismissals are also an IPL record.The captaincy record grew alongside those performances. Dhoni led CSK in 235 IPL matches, winning 136, and took the franchise to 10 finals as captain. Five of those ended with the trophy in his hands - 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023. He also led CSK to Champions League T20 titles in 2010 and 2014.The numbers place him at the top of several IPL leaderboards. But for CSK, the story was also about the continuity: the same captain returning after a suspension, rebuilding after difficult seasons, trusting players in pressure situations and taking the team back to the final stages year after year. Across 18 IPL seasons, he scored 4,865 runs in 248 matches for the franchise. The association outlasted changing teams, changing roles and changing generations of supporters.A captain measured beyond seasons and trophiesAnd then there are the people who made the journey their own. Nabeel had said in 2023 that he knew Dhoni was entering the last phase of his playing career. “It's his last phase. I don't know if this is his last season or not, but it's the last phase. So we have to make this season more memorable.”That season has now passed, and the playing chapter is over. Dhoni will remain with CSK in a mentoring role, but the sight of him walking out in the yellow jersey, with a game hanging in the balance, belongs to the past.The No. 7 jersey will no longer be worn, but the whistles, the yellow flags and the memories of those evenings when Dhoni walked out to bat with a game hanging in the balance will endure. CSK may be moving into a new chapter, but the man who shaped its identity will forever remain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'We need to block outside noise': Morne Morkel's message to Team India ahead of first Test vs New Zealand
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Team India bowling coach Morne Morkel wants his players to focus on their game and not get distracted by outside talk as they prepare for the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Team India bowling coach Morne Morkel wants his players to focus on their game and not get distracted by outside talk as they prepare for the first Test against New Zealand, starting Thursday.With conditions at Basin Reserve in Wellington expected to test both teams, India are considering playing four fast bowlers.However, Morkel said the final decision would be taken after assessing the conditions."Conditions allow us to have that kind of mindset, playing four seamers. We will take a look at the conditions and take the final call," Morkel said during the press conference ahead of the opening Test.Both teams will also have to deal with the challenge of strong winds, which can make life difficult for fast bowlers. Morkel, however, wants his players to be mentally prepared for what lies ahead."Both teams will face the challenge of the wind. The boys know what they are in for. It’s about having a strong mindset. Expect our guys to have the body language of still wanting the ball. We need to block outside noise and play the game of cricket and not overthink the conditions," he said.Gill confirms four fast bowlers, India yet to finalise combinationIndia captain Shubman Gill had earlier confirmed that the team would "for sure" play four fast bowlers in the two-Test series against New Zealand."We will be playing four fast bowlers for sure," Gill declared ahead of the series."All our fast bowlers have done well and it is a good headache to have," he said, referring to the impressive performance of India's young pace attack in the recent ODI series, which the visitors won 3-1.The return of senior pacer Jasprit Bumrah has further strengthened India's pace attack. Gurnoor Brar, who impressed in the white-ball series, has also been retained in the squad at the expense of spinner Kuldeep Yadav.However, Gill made it clear that the team management was yet to decide which four pacers would make the playing XI."We want four fast bowlers but don't know which ones (will play). From day three, we have seen that the pitch gets flat and we need someone who can hit the deck," Gill said.Akash Deep and Prasidh Krishna are expected to be among the leading contenders for a place in the pace attack. Anshul Kamboj has also caught the attention of head coach Gautam Gambhir and bowling coach Morkel during the team's preparations.India keeping World Test Championship final in mindIndia have given priority to the two-Test series and made changes to their ODI plans to ensure that players selected for the longer format get enough time to prepare. The team management pulled players out of the ODI assignments to allow them to acclimatise to the conditions and focus on Test cricket.Gill said the series carries significant importance in India's bid to qualify for the World Test Championship final."If we win these two Tests, there is a very good chance of playing the WTC final. Hence, we pulled out all players from ODIs to give them the best chance of preparation," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: Will Mohammed Siraj play first Test against New Zealand? Morne Morkel leaves final call to Shubman Gill
articles.summary: India bowling coach Morne Morkel did not give a clear answer on Mohammed Siraj's place in the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand, saying
articles.body: India bowling coach Morne Morkel did not give a clear answer on Mohammed Siraj's place in the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand, saying the final decision rests with captain Shubman Gill.With questions being raised about Siraj's recent form, Morkel was asked whether the fast bowler's place in the team was under scrutiny. However, the bowling coach backed Siraj's abilities and left the selection call to the captain."Siraj is a world-class performer, whenever he has stepped in India jersey, whenever he has played," Morkel said on the eve of the first Test.He also made it clear that he was confident about India's bowling resources and believed the attack had enough firepower to take 20 wickets."My feedback to Gautam (head coach Gautam Gambhir) was that we have enough in attack to take 20 wickets. Ultimately the call will be taken by Shubman," he said.'Don't overthink conditions'Morkel also warned the bowlers against thinking too much about the conditions. He wants them to trust their plans and focus on executing them rather than getting distracted by the pitch or the weather."Don't overthink conditions," Morkel said.He believes getting off to a strong start will be important, but also pointed out that a Test match can change at any stage. India will need bowlers who can make an impact not just in the opening sessions but also towards the end of the game."The best way of winning is to set the tone in the first session, but the first session doesn't always win a Test. You need guys who can produce a magical spell on the fourth or fifth day," he added.'We cannot afford to lose points': MorkelMorkel urged the Indian bowlers to ignore external distractions and concentrate on their plans. With India competing for a place in next year's World Test Championship final, he stressed that the team cannot afford to drop points.India are currently fourth in the World Test Championship standings and will be looking to make the most of the two-Test series against New Zealand."We need to block outside noise and get the ball in the right areas. We cannot afford to lose points. The team needs to take ownership and get quicker to the mark. The responsibility lies with the bowler and the captain," he said.Morkel also spoke about the challenges of bowling in Wellington, where strong winds can affect the fast bowlers. He explained that bowling against the wind can help generate movement, but bowlers need to make adjustments to their approach."When you bowl into the wind, you get a bit of shape. Your thought process is important. You can hold your actions a bit longer," he said.He added that the wind was not as strong as it had been in recent weeks. The Indian bowlers, therefore, would need to keep assessing the conditions and adjust their lengths during the match.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Mentor’ Singh Dhoni shifts from behind stumps to behind the scenes
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Last Saturday, as Mahendra Singh Dhoni was discussing the Chennai Super Kings retention list for the forthcoming IPL with the team management, he
articles.body: CHENNAI: Last Saturday, as Mahendra Singh Dhoni was discussing the Chennai Super Kings retention list for the forthcoming IPL with the team management, he dropped a bombshell. Towards the end of the discussion, the legend said, “You should probably add my name to the list of released players.”In her own words, team owner Rupa Gurnath was “stunned”. “Both me and (CSK chief executive officer) Kasi Viswanathan could not believe what we were hearing. The video call froze for a moment and I told MS that even the internet can’t handle this,” Rupa said in a message on the franchise’s website on Tuesday.It was a huge blow for all those CSK die-hards who were hoping to see their beloved Thala in action for one last time. “But Dhoni will always be a part of us and will be the team mentor,” Rupa added.‘Not playing a single game last season played on MSD’s mind’That little tweak in the field, the last-over heroics and most importantly, the imposing presence on the field — all the things that made MS Dhoni special will now become memories. But CSK is determined to add to the legend of the No. 7 shirt that Dhoni donned for 19 years. The jersey will be retired for the Men in Yellow.“There is no CSK without Dhoni. For nearly two decades, we have walked and grown alongside each other, through triumphs, setbacks and everything in between,” N Srinivasan, the former supremo of CSK, said in a statement.Dhoni retired from international cricket six years ago. Since then, his sole aim was to see CSK being on top of the IPL charts. But performances nosedived since 2023 as CSK failed to make the last-four stage three years in a row. Dhoni, too, was unable to recreate the old magic with the bat.But Dhoni’s promise to the CSK fans a few years ago that he would play his last IPL game at the MA Chidambaram Stadium still gave the management hope. Till a fortnight ago, any query on Dhoni’s availability to the CSK hierarchy would meet the same response: “Of course he will play this year.”The 45-year-old, though, didn’t commit. Rupa revealed that a few months ago, Dhoni had told her that it could be a little difficult for him to play the season. Sources close to the developments told TOI that it was all about the state of his body that made Dhoni push towards the decision to hang up his boots. “He couldn’t play a single game last season and that played on his mind. There were still a few niggles and he didn’t practise at all after the 2026 IPL,” a source said.But as Dhoni slowly gave up on the idea of playing another season, he dived deep into team building. He knew that the team had to be rebuilt if they want to have a fighting chance in the forthcoming IPL season. Every decision that was made over the course of the last couple of months — from letting coach Stephen Fleming go to the appointment of Zaheer Khan to a complete revamp of the support staff — he oversaw everything.In the last couple of years, he had taken a bit of a backseat in the team-building process. But now that the team was looking to fight back, it was pivotal that he takes a lead role. “It is his call whether he will be present in the auction. But of course, he will play a very important role,” COO Viswanathan said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: MS Dhoni: Chennai’s Own! Like Rajini, an adopted son gave the fans as much love as he received
articles.summary: Chennai always loved its cricket, just that it never had its Super King. Till MS Dhoni happened.
articles.body: Chennai always loved its cricket, just that it never had its Super King. Till MS Dhoni happened.In 2007, as the IPL was conceptualized, franchises across the country were busy getting their ‘icon players’ into their squads. Mumbai had Sachin Tendulkar, Kolkata had Sourav Ganguly while Bengaluru boasted of Rahul Dravid. But Chennai didn’t have one. And that’s when N Srinivasan, mainstay of India Cements — the then owners of Chennai Super Kings — decided to bring in Dhoni from the auction.It wasn’t without a contest. KKR went hard for the Jharkhand cricketer — but they simply didn’t have the purse that CSK had reserved for Dhoni. “He had just won the T20 World Cup, it was a no-brainer that we would go for him. Of course, we never thought he would become the success that became, but his commitment always attracted us,” Srinivasan once told TOI.Chennai has had its share of cricket stars in former India captains Srinivas Venkataraghavan and Krishnamachari Srikkanth. But what it lacked was the runaway success that makes a sportsman the king of the hearts. “That’s exactly where Dhoni comes in,” Srikkanth, part of early-day CSK management, told TOI. “The people of Chennai started to identify success in cricket with Dhoni as CSK went on its trophy winning run. That’s how the aura of Dhoni happened.”The Dhoni-Chennai love affair was almost instant. In 2008, the IPL, a revolutionary sporting idea that immediately exploded into the imagination of a nation at large, found a welcoming home in Chennai, the mostly sedate southern city.For Dhoni, it was a quiet stardom that was previously reserved for film stars and filmstars-turned-politicians. Pictures of him riding his bike into the hotel for a CSK press conference would hog the newly-begun entertainment supplements of newspapers. The timing of it all seemed almost manipulated. Suddenly, Chennai had a sporting hero of their own, India’s captain.In the league’s inaugural season, an improbable run to the final followed. The following season, a last-four berth and the first title in 2010. The Jharkhand bomber had completely taken over Chennai the way a Marathi bus conductor from Karnataka — Rajinikanth — conquered Chennai hearts way back in the 1980s.“In many ways, Dhoni’s superstardom can be equated with Rajini’s. It shows the openness of Chennai’s people. They are always ready to appreciate talent,” Srikkanth said.The success got sweeter through the early 2010s as CSK again became champion in 2011 and was almost a permanent fixture in the final. Dhoni was at the centre of it all.That is, until the 2013 spotfixing scandal led to CSK’s dismissal after the 2015 edition. The obits were written and everybody was convinced that it would never be the same again for the Chennai franchise. Dhoni may have turned out for Pune Supergiants for those two years of the ban, but always maintained: “Chennai will always be my first home.”Paradoxically, it was in these two years of ‘exile’ that the cult of Dhoni grew in the hearts of the CSK fans. In fact, by 2018 when Dhoni was back in the CSK yellow, it seemed that IPL itself was waiting for it. Dhoni, in his No. 7 jersey, became the image of brand IPL’s growth and its ability to stave off its detractors.Dhoni’s arc from 2018 onwards to help CSK win back its glory days stumped everybody, barring Srinivasan. He assembled a ‘dad’s army’ and when many found the 30-plus picks like Shane Watson, Imran Tahir, Harbhajan Singh, Ambati Rayudu, Faf du Plessis as defying sporting logic, Srinivasan held firm. “We know what Dhoni is doing and we believe in it. A combination of experience and ability is gold dust, just see what happens,” he said.What followed were three titles in six years — CSK’s golden era and Dhoni’s high noon. His manoeuvrings on the field, the ability to conjure lastover sixes and bowling changes made it a five-all in the title count with Mumbai Indians. But on the sidelines, there was a revolution brewing in T20 cricket. Despite his tactical brilliance, he probably missed a trick as the game moved on from methodical madness to monstrous power.‘Brand CSK’ has struck its lowest ebb over the last three years — three back-to-back failures to make the last-four is unthinkable by their own lofty standards. Injuries have taken a toll on the maestro’s body and despite his initial assurance that he would play this season, the 45-year-old has opted out.But make no mistake, he is leading CSK’s revival. Everything is being overseen by Dhoni. The competition is now more demanding, tougher.Dhoni, the mastermind, will be there in the dugout mentoring his new bunch.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: India stars Rohit Sharma and Jasprit Bumrah have paid tribute to MS Dhoni after the legendary wicketkeeper-batter's IPL playing career came to an end.The two cricketers took to social media to congratulate Dhoni and share their memories of playing alongside him. Dhoni has been one of the biggest names in the tournament since its first edition in 2008.Rohit posted a picture with Dhoni on X and recalled the time they spent together on the field."Congratulations on an incredible IPL career, Dhoni bhai. It's been fun sharing the field and so many memories with you over the years. Much respect!," Rohit posted on X.Bumrah also shared a picture with the former India captain and described him as his favourite cricketer, someone he had always looked up to."My favourite cricket player and the person I looked upto the most thank you for all the memories and lots of wishes for what lies ahead," Bumrah wrote while sharing a picture with Dhoni.Dhoni to take up new role as CSK mentorChennai Super Kings (CSK), the franchise Dhoni represented for 17 seasons, announced on Tuesday that he would take up the role of Team Mentor ahead of the IPL 2027 season.The announcement brings an end to Dhoni's remarkable playing career in the IPL. He has been associated with the tournament since its inaugural edition and has remained one of its biggest attractions.Over the years, Dhoni established himself as one of the competition's most successful captains and a reliable finisher. His leadership and performances also played a key role in CSK's success.Apart from CSK, Dhoni also played for Rising Pune Supergiant in the 2016 and 2017 seasons, when Chennai Super Kings were suspended from the tournament.He returned to CSK in 2018 and led the franchise to the IPL title in his first season back.Dhoni's final IPL appearance came in 2025Dhoni handed over the CSK captaincy to Ruturaj Gaikwad ahead of the 2024 season, marking a change in the team's leadership. However, he continued to play an important role in the side, contributing with his experience behind the stumps and his finishing skills.His last IPL appearance was against Gujarat Titans during the 2025 season. He missed the 2026 edition due to a calf injury. The latest announcement confirms that he will not return to the field as a player.Dhoni's IPL numbersDhoni ended his IPL career with 278 matches and 5,439 runs at an average of 38.30 and a strike rate of 137.45.His record also includes 24 half-centuries and 264 sixes. He remained one of the IPL's most reliable middle-order batters and finishers throughout his career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cricket Australia sets up 'safe space' for players to share sandpapergate experiences
articles.summary: The 2018 scandal has resurfaced this month after Usman Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about the cheating plot.
articles.body:
Cricket Australia has launched an independent "forum" for players and staff involved in the sandpapergate scandal to share their version of events.

In a memoir released earlier this month, former player Usman Khawaja claimed the entire Australia team knew of the plot to tamper with the ball during a 2018 Test in South Africa, contradicting the investigation at the time.

His comments have led to a bitter split among former and current players and have overshadowed the beginning of Australia's international cricket season.

The forum was not a new investigation and there will be no new penalties, Cricket Australia said, adding that nobody would be forced to take part.

However, chief executive Todd Greenberg said he hoped the discussions would allow the sport to "move on".

"The game is genuinely hurting at the moment. It's not good for anyone," he said.

"We need to find a path through and we need some time to heal."

The sandpapergate scandal is often described as one of Australian cricket's darkest days and was a source of national shame.

Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'

Whole Australia team knew of sandpaper use - Khawaja

An expedited investigation at the time found three players knew about the plan: captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft. They all faced lengthy bans.

However Khawaja, Warner and another player on the tour, Chadd Sayers, have all now said they believe everyone knew.

Current Australia captain Pat Cummins has rejected claims he knew sandpaper was being taken onto the field as "nonsense" , and expressed hurt that Khawaja - his friend - had called his reputation into question.

The release of Khawaja's book has also renewed scrutiny of Cricket Australia's initial investigation. A handful of players - including the batter - have said they were not interviewed for it, and Warner has accused the governing body of a "cover-up" .

"Over the past week we've had several different and conflicting accounts of what transpired in Cape Town in 2018 and it's been an incredibly difficult and uncomfortable time for the game and for everyone who was involved," Greenberg said on Wednesday.

"What's become clear is that some players were not heard at that time. That opportunity now exists in a place without judgement, without sanction."

Terms of reference for the forum are being drafted, he said, and a former judge or "someone of that ilk" will be recruited to run it, confidentially and independently.

No deadline has been set, but Greenberg said he hoped the discussions could be completed "quickly", at which time the Cricket Australia board would decide what information to make public.

"We will look to be as transparent as we possibly can, whilst at the same time protecting the confidentiality of the people who come forward."

The incident had "a lot to do with the culture that existed back at the time", Greenberg said: a win-at-all-costs mentality which he admitted the governing body played a role in creating.

He added that it is important the current Australian team be "afforded the space to perform at their best at what is a very important time and period for the game".

Though players like Khawaja and Warner have retired from international cricket, Australia's bowling attack in the contentious third Test - Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon and Mitchell Starc - remain fixtures in the national side. So too does Steve Smith, who returned to the team in 2019.

Khawaja, who is commentating Australia's one-day international against England in Hobart on Wednesday alongside Warner, welcomed the announcement.

"I wish Cricket Australia would have done this a week-and-a-half ago, probably longer ago," Khawaja said on streamer Kayo Sports.

"My questions will always be 'what is the outcome from this?'"

Warner said Australians deserved an "open public inquiry" instead.

"Because we have no idea about what's happened behind closed doors with CA [Cricket Australia]."

Former player turned coach Jason Gillespie and Darren Lehmann - who coached Australia at the time of the scandal - both said the forum was a good idea.

"Let's not beat around the bush - they didn't have a choice. Cricket Australia had to do something, the drums were beating louder and louder," Gillespie told the broadcaster ABC.

"I haven't been great and the people close to me know that... The last couple of weeks have been tough, but they have been for everyone," Lehmann added.

articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: Beware the Basin bluff! Shubman Gill's four-pacer plan looks beyond the first morning
articles.summary: The first thing that catches the eye at the Basin Reserve is the grass. Lots of it. On the banks and the outfield and plenty of it on the pitch too.
articles.body: The first thing that catches the eye at the Basin Reserve is the grass. Lots of it. On the banks and the outfield and plenty of it on the pitch too. The curators have left close to 15mm of cover on the surface, significantly more than the usual 6-8mm one is used to seeing at the start of Tests at most venues. It might create the impression of a classic seamer’s paradise ahead of Thursday’s first Test.Yet India seem to be wary of falling into that trap.Captain Shubman Gill, while speaking to the media, made repeated references to wanting bowlers who can “hit the deck hard”. It suggests the visitors want to plan for what the pitch could become on days three, four and five rather than just what it might offer in the opening session.“We’ve seen that on days three, four and five, especially with the old ball, the wicket can go a little flat,” Gill said while discussing team combinations.It is a view backed by history. While the Basin Reserve can provide movement under cloud cover early in the match, the surface often settles down considerably as the game progresses, with batting becoming easier once the lacquer fades off the Kookaburra ball and the green grass on the pitch changes to a straw-coloured stubble.Could that explain why Gill is thinking also about durability rather than just swing and seam?“We need at least a couple of bowlers who can hit the deck hard and bowl in the high-130s or 140-plus range. Once the Kookaburra ball gets old, the seam wears down and it doesn’t move as much off the pitch. That’s when you need bowlers who can hit the deck hard and keep creating chances.”The captain’s views provide clues about what India’s pace attack could be come Thursday.It’s clear India will play four fast bowlers, the selection debate described as “a headache, but a good kind of headache.”Under Gill and Gambhir, India have also valued lower-order runs, and that is why we have seen players like Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar play overseas with Ravindra Jadeja as all-round options, with batting being the stronger suit of all three cricketers.However, when discussing the lower-order balance, Gill on Tuesday highlighted Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj for their batting abilities. It probably suggests a change of tactic.“Ideally, we’re looking at seven proper batsmen. The No. 8 and No. 9 spots will depend on the combination because Akash can bat a bit, Anshul can bat a bit.”Join the dots and what do you get? Not a happy picture if you happen to be Mohammed Siraj.While Siraj remains one of India’s most experienced seamers and a proven new-ball operator, who helped India draw the series in England with a heroic performance at the Oval, Gill’s emphasis on lower-order runs, height, pace and second-innings effectiveness appears to favour bowlers such as Akash Deep, Kamboj and the rapid Gurnoor over a like-for-like seam option to support Jasprit Bumrah and Prasidh Krishna.Gill also acknowledged the unique wind factor of Wellington. “I think it’s actually tougher for the bowlers than the batters. If a bowler has to send down 15 or 20 overs and half of them are against the wind, it’s a very tough job.”That probably explains India’s desire for a varied attack capable of operating in different phases of the game. Gill was in the reserves six years ago when New Zealand exposed India at the Basin because man to man, they were better equipped for the conditions.As captain, he does not want a repeat. “They were better prepared and knew exactly how to exploit our weaknesses. That’s one reason we’re looking at four fast bowlers. You want bowlers who can exploit movement if it’s there and others who can bend their backs and hit hard lengths consistently if the ball isn’t doing much.”And that is why the final XI may be decided less by what the Basin Reserve looks like on Wednesday than by what Gill expects it to look like on Sunday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: This is your captain speaking: From reluctant leader to commanding voice, Shubman Gill is reshaping India's Test culture
articles.summary: When the captaincy was thrust upon Shubman Gill after a tumultuous Test tour of Australia and before India embarked on the tour of England in 2025 to play
articles.body: When the captaincy was thrust upon Shubman Gill after a tumultuous Test tour of Australia and before India embarked on the tour of England in 2025 to play five Tests, there were doubts about whether the soft-spoken batter was ready for the burden. Barring leadership exposure in IPL for Gujarat Titans, he did not have much to show on his CV in terms of leadership.The elegant Punjab batter, though, answered the biggest question in the only way possible: with runs. A staggering 754-run series in England established him as a batter capable of carrying the weight of expectation. Swayed by that, the selectors appointed him as ODI captain too.Cut to a year later. Gill has now evolved into a leader comfortable taking ownership of decisions, defending teammates publicly and laying down a broader vision for Indian Test cricket.Ahead of the first Test in Wellington, Gill’s words revealed a captain consumed by the format that matters most to him, much like the man he idolises, Virat Kohli.ALSO READ: Beware the Basin bluff! Shubman Gill's four-pacer plan looks beyond the first morning“If someone had asked me a month ago which of the three series I’d most like to win, it would definitely have been the Test series,” Gill said, addressing the media at the Basin Reserve in wet and windy Wellington on Tuesday, two days prior to the start of the two-match Test series vs New Zealand.“We’re very happy to have won the T20I and ODI series, but there’s nothing like winning the Test series as well,” the skipper stressed.The remark was telling. In ODIs, Gill, despite being the No. 1 batter in the format and the captain, still operates in the shadows of Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma, two giants who continue to define the format and drive the narrative. In T20Is, despite once being viewed as a future leadership option and serving as Suryakumar Yadav’s deputy, team balance and combinations pushed him out of the squad all together ahead of the T20 World Cup.But Test cricket has become Gill’s domain.It is in the longest format that he has made the most consequential decisions as captain. Over the last year, Gill has repeatedly stressed the importance of adequate preparation before Test assignments.“Whenever we get the opportunity, I’d like our preparation to be as thorough as possible,” Gill said. “It’s not easy coming into a different time zone, adjusting your body clock, adapting to the conditions and dealing with the physical and mental stress that comes with it. An extra three or four days definitely helps.”The same conviction was evident in the way he backed Rishabh Pant. Despite Pant’s occasionally uneasy equation with coach Gautam Gambhir and his removal as vice-captain, Gill emphatically endorsed the value that the mercurial wicketkeeper-batter brings to the team in SENA countries. “He’s probably one of the most experienced and senior contenders in the team,” Gill said, adding that Pant has played over 50 Tests. “Given the quality he brings, he’s scored hundreds all over the world. He’s got hundreds in Australia, South Africa and England. This is probably the only country where he hasn’t.”Gill has tied his leadership goals to India’s World Test Championship ambitions. He has been part of the 2025 Champions Trophy and 2023 and 2025 Asia Cup wins and Border-Gavaskar Trophy triumphs in 2021 and 2023. But he has also played in two WTC finals that India lost in 2021 and 2023, where he could not contribute much as an opener.It remains unfinished business for him.“I believe if we win these two Test matches, we have a very good chance of making the World Test Championship final,” he said. “That’s why we pulled most of the players out of the ODI side early so they could have the best preparation possible.”If India can secure a place in the WTC final and ultimately lift the mace, Gill’s impact will be measured beyond just his numbers with the bat.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket Australia (CA) has announced plans to establish an independent forum for players and support staff involved in the controversial 2018 tour of
articles.body: Cricket Australia (CA) has announced plans to establish an independent forum for players and support staff involved in the controversial 2018 tour of South Africa, offering them an opportunity to share their versions of events in a confidential and respectful environment as the fallout from the ball-tampering scandal resurfaces.The decision comes in the wake of fresh allegations in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, which have reignited the debate over how much the Australian dressing room knew about the infamous sandpaper incident in Cape Town. CA interim chairman David Boon said the forum would allow those involved to share their experiences and perspectives, nearly nine years after the scandal rocked Australian cricket.However, the governing body has made it clear that the initiative will not reopen its original investigation, nor will it lead to fresh sanctions. CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said the forum was intended to give everyone who wished to speak an independent, safe and private platform.'Time for a circuit breaker': Boon explains CA's decisionAnnouncing the board's decision in Hobart on Wednesday, ahead of Australia's one-day international against England, Boon said the prolonged controversy had become a distraction for the sport."The CA Board agreed to establish a forum that will allow players and staff involved in the events of South Africa in 2018 to share their experiences and their perspectives," Boon told reporters."For almost a decade, the fallout from these events has remained part of conversation around Australian cricket ... We believe it is time for a circuit breaker."In its official statement, CA said the forum would allow those who wished to come forward to share their recollections in a confidential environment. The board has opted against initiating a fresh investigation, believing that a forum would provide a better opportunity for everyone involved to speak constructively and with mutual respect.Boon stressed that the exercise was not about reopening old wounds but about allowing people to be heard."This forum is not about relitigating the past. It is about creating an opportunity for those who wish to be heard to tell their stories in a respectful environment, and for our sport to listen," he said.The former Australia batter also highlighted the importance of restoring relationships within the cricket fraternity."As a former player, I know that one of the most important things cricket gives us is the relationships we build and the mateship that endures long after playing careers end. My hope is that this process can help strengthen those connections and allow us to focus on what lies ahead," Boon added.Khawaja's claims reopen old woundsThe latest controversy follows claims in Khawaja's autobiography that contradicted the findings of CA's original investigation into the ball-tampering episode during the third Test against South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018.The initial probe concluded that only then captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opening batter Cameron Bancroft were aware of the plan to use sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball.Bancroft was caught on television cameras attempting to scuff up the ball with a piece of sandpaper, triggering one of the biggest controversies in Australian cricket history.Khawaja's account, backed by Warner, suggested that the wider team was at least aware of the attempt to tamper with the ball. However, Test captain Pat Cummins and fellow fast bowler Mitchell Starc have maintained that they knew nothing about the plan.The revelations have once again brought the contrasting accounts of those involved into focus, prompting CA to provide an avenue for players and support staff who were not interviewed during the original investigation to share their recollections.'The game is hurting': Greenberg rules out fresh investigationGreenberg acknowledged that the latest developments had created an uncomfortable situation for Australian cricket, while also accepting that the governing body had a role in shaping the culture that existed at the time."Over the past week we have heard several different and conflicting accounts of what transpired in Cape Town in 2018. This has been an incredibly difficult and uncomfortable time for the game and all those involved," he said."What happened then and continues to play out now has a lot to do with the culture that existed at that time. A culture that CA played a part in creating."He also pointed to the Ethics Centre report commissioned after the scandal and the subsequent adoption of 36 of its 42 recommendations as part of the governing body's efforts to address cultural shortcomings.Greenberg said the new forum was an opportunity to give everyone a voice without turning it into another disciplinary exercise."This is a chance to give everyone a voice in an independent, safe and private setting," he said."This is not a re-investigation, it is not designed to reprosecute or sanction."Participation will be entirely voluntary, with no player or support staff member compelled to come forward. CA also does not intend to make the findings or accounts necessarily public."Let's be honest - the game is hurting at the moment," Greenberg said."It is not good for anyone. We need to find a path through and we need to heal."The bans that shook Australian cricketThe 2018 ball-tampering scandal resulted in severe penalties for the three players identified by CA's original investigation. Smith and Warner were each handed 12-month bans from elite cricket for bringing the game into disrepute, while Bancroft received a nine-month suspension for his role in carrying the sandpaper onto the field.The episode also led to widespread scrutiny of Australia's team culture and prompted significant changes within the governing body.Eight years on, CA hopes the independent forum will help bring closure to a controversy that continues to divide opinions and affect those associated with the game."We hope everyone will respect this process and the players will be given the space they need to perform at their best during an important period for the game," Greenberg said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Is Cricket Australia re-opening investigation into Sandpapergate? CA announces new 'forum' as Usman Khawaja expresses concern
articles.summary: Is Cricket Australia reopening the Sandpapergate investigation? CA ruled out a fresh probe and launched a new forum after Usman Khawaja's book claims.
articles.body:
Cricket Australia has set up a new forum linked to the 2018 Cape Town incident.

Usman Khawaja's book triggered the move, and several former colleagues have rejected his claims.

The board insists this is not a fresh inquiry, yet Khawaja still has doubts.

What is Cricket Australia's new Sandpapergate forum? Everything explained

Cricket Australia has stepped back into one of the most uncomfortable chapters in its recent history, and the way it has done so has left many people asking what the board is really trying to achieve. The governing body announced on Wednesday that it will create a forum for those connected with the 2018 sandpaper incident in South Africa.

Interim chair David Boon and chief executive Todd Greenberg made the announcement at Bellerive Oval, a little more than an hour before the third ODI between Australia and England was due to begin.

The board had met the night before and agreed on the plan, which allows players and staff who were involved in the events of that tour to share their experiences.

The decision comes only days after Usman Khawaja made a series of allegations about the Cape Town incident in his autobiography, Sabr, which was published last week. His claims drew responses from captain Pat Cummins and others, and they have kept a subject that many in Australian cricket hoped was behind them in the headlines.

According to the board, the forum will be confidential, and it will be open to anyone who was present at the time, although nobody will be forced to take part. An independent person will be appointed in the coming days, along with the terms of reference, and CA will decide later how much of the process is made public.

Boon stressed that the aim is not to go back over the incident but to let those involved share their recollections as part of a push to move forward.

"Last night, the Cricket Australia Board met, and we reached a decision that we believe is in the best interests of the game," Boon said. "After careful discussion, we agreed to establish a forum that will allow players and staff involved in the events of South Africa in 2018 to share their experiences and their perspectives."

The interim chair then described how the long-running debate has affected the sport, which he said has become a distraction over time.

He added: "For almost a decade, the fallout from these events, or from those events, has remained part of the conversation around Australian cricket. It has been a difficult chapter for many people, and increasingly, the ongoing debate has become a distraction for our game. We believe it is time for a circuit breaker."

Boon repeated that the forum is not intended to revisit the past in a legal sense, and he closed with a call for unity.

"This forum is not about re-litigating the past at all. It's about creating an opportunity for those who wish to be heard to tell their stories in a respectful, safe environment, and for our sport to listen."

"Australian cricket is at its strongest when we're united, and we owe it to everyone who loves the game to make every reasonable effort to move forward together with understanding, respect, and perspective."

Is Cricket Australia re-opening the Sandpapergate investigation? Greenberg's answer

The short answer from the board is no. Greenberg confirmed that the original 2018 investigation will neither be reopened nor made public, with confidentiality given as the reason.

Greenberg said the game is hurting right now, and then spoke about the need to recover.

"It's not good for anyone. We need to find a path through, and we need some time to heal."

He also made clear what the new process is and is not meant to do, and he repeated that taking part is a personal choice.

He said: "As part of this process, and so that all parties who wish to can tell their version of events, we have set up now an independent forum. It's a chance to give everyone a voice in an independent and a safe setting. It's not a re-investigation. It's not designed to re-prosecute or to sanction."

"No one is compelled to participate. It is entirely up to each individual. It's important to remember we're talking about events that happened eight and a half years ago, and I hope everyone will respect this process."

Usman Khawaja and David Warner react to Cricket Australia's Sandpapergate forum

Khawaja welcomed the idea of a safe space but told Kayo Sports that he still has questions about the forum. He wants the public to hear the full story, and he believes that is impossible unless every person involved speaks.

He said: "I have always wanted a safe space to chat… I also have some questions about Cricket Australia because the public wants to know what happened there. It's hard to get the whole truth unless everyone is speaking."

He then said he does not want to see anyone punished, and he raised a concern about what the board will do with the material.

He further asked: "I don't think there should be any sanctions… the board makes the decisions but what comes out at the end? I have a really good relationship with Todd Greenberg, and I respect what he's trying to do there.

"But at the end of the day if you're going to cherry-pick what is said in this report, the board can choose whatever they want to come in, or come out. Are we just going in a circle here? That's the thing I'm not sure about."

Warner, who was speaking alongside Khawaja, also ruled out any desire for further penalties. He pointed to what the players accepted at the time and to what he sees as the real purpose of the forum.

He said: "We put our hands up, we accepted what Cricket Australia handed out to us. It's not about penalties. It's about transparency and accountability - which Todd's acknowledged, on CA's behalf, about the culture at the time with the players and CA."

A forum without a published outcome may not settle the Sandpapergate debate

The board's intention is easy to understand, because nearly a decade of argument has simply worn people down. A confidential, voluntary forum offers a way for everyone to speak without the threat of sanctions, and that is a reasonable starting point.

However, the same features that make the forum safe may also limit its value. Khawaja has already pointed out the central weakness: CA will decide what is released at the end. If the public sees only a short summary, those who want answers are likely to treat it as a polished version of events, and the debate will carry on.

The voluntary nature of the process is a second problem. Cummins and Starc have strongly rejected Khawaja's version, and if they choose not to take part, the forum will hear one side of the dispute far more than the other. A discussion with missing voices is unlikely to produce the shared understanding Boon hopes for.

CA can improve its chances by publishing the terms of reference early, by naming a respected independent figure, and by being clear about what will be shared. The board has said it wants a circuit breaker, but a breaker only works if people trust it. That trust will depend on how openly the process is run.

articles.title: IPL Retentions: Mitchell Starc, Travis Head lead high-profile IPL releases
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Australia pacer Mitchell Starc and batter Travis Head were among the biggest names released by their IPL franchises on Tuesday, the retention
articles.body: MUMBAI: Australia pacer Mitchell Starc and batter Travis Head were among the biggest names released by their IPL franchises on Tuesday, the retention deadline, ahead of the Dec 16 auction in Goa. Both players are understood to have opted out of IPL2027 because of workload concerns. Australia host New Zealand in four Tests from Dec, tour India for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Jan and play the 150th Ashes anniversary Test in March. The IPL will be followed by the World Test Championship final, if Australia qualify, and a five-Test Ashes series in England.DC released Starc, freeing Rs 11.75 crore. The pacer had returned to the IPL in 2024 after a nine-year gap but missed the first half of the 2026 season under CA’s workload-management plan. DC released 10 players, including Nitish Rana, Abhishek Porel, Ben Duckett, Dushmantha Chameera and Karun Nair.Sunrisers Hyderabad released Head, who had formed a destructive opening pair with Abhishek Sharma. Head, signed for 14 cr, was among nine players let go by SRH, along with Gerald Coetzee and Jaydev Unadkat.Fast bowlers dominate release listMumbai Indians parted with Trent Boult and Deepak Chahar, freeing 21.75 cr. Lucknow Super Giants released Avesh Khan, Anrich Nortje and Matthew Breetzke, while Rajasthan Royals let go of Shimron Hetmyer, Tushar Deshpande, Adam Milne, Kwena Maphaka and Kuldeep Sen.KKR released 12 players, including Ajinkya Rahane, Rachin Ravindra, Akash Deep, Mustafizur Rahman and Matheesha Pathirana. KKR retained Australian allrounder Cameron Green, the most expensive player at the 2026 auction at Rs 25.2 cr.Chennai Super Kings released 10 players on the day MS Dhoni announced his IPL retirement. Uttar Pradesh allrounder Prashant Veer, bought for 14.2 crore, was the costliest player released. CSK also let go of Matthew Short and Matt Henry.RCB retain Yash DayalRCB, meanwhile, released six players, including injured England batter Jacob Bethell, but retained Yash Dayal for Rs 5 cr. Punjab Kings released six players, including Lockie Ferguson, Mitch Owen and Nehal Wadhera, while retaining Marcus Stoinis despite acquiring Hardik Pandya from MI.TOP FIVE BIG-MONEY CASUALTIESPrashant Veer (CSK; freed up Rs 14.2 cr)Travis Head (SRH; Rs 14 cr)Matheesha Pathirana (KKR; Rs 13 cr)Trent Boult (MI; Rs 12.5 cr)Mitchell Starc (DC; Rs 11.75 cr)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: MS Dhoni’s IPL moments: 19 seasons, countless memories – Seven moments that defined the CSK legend
articles.summary: MS Dhoni's remarkable IPL journey came to an end after 19 seasons, with Chennai Super Kings leaving the 45-year-old out of their retention list ahead of
articles.body: MS Dhoni's remarkable IPL journey came to an end after 19 seasons, with Chennai Super Kings leaving the 45-year-old out of their retention list ahead of the 2027 players' auction and listing him as a team mentor.Having last featured in IPL 2025 before missing the 2026 season due to a knee injury, the former India captain leaves behind a legacy filled with unforgettable moments, defining performances and enduring memories.FIRST TITLE, 2010: On April 25, CSK beat MI by 22 runs in the final, marking the moment Dhoni established CSK as a major force and setting the stage for a successful title defence in 2011.FINAL-OVER MIRACLE, 2016: Playing for RPSG during CSK’s two-year suspension, MSD produced a stunning finish against Kings XI Punjab. With Pune needing 23 from the final over, Dhoni hit Axar Patel for 2 sixes and a four before sealing a 4-wicket win with a last-ball six. He scored 64* off 32.COMEBACK KING, 2018: Questions were raised whether the franchise could regain old identity. Dhoni answered emphatically, with CSK chasing down 206 against RCB, recovering from 74/4 to win by 5 wickets. Dhoni remained unbeaten on 70 off 34. CSK went on to win the title.LOSING HIS COOL, 2019: During a tense finish against Rajasthan Royals in Jaipur on April 11, Dhoni stormed onto the field to challenge the umpires after a waist-high full toss was called a no-ball before the decision was reversed. He was fined 50% of his match fee.BEST KNOCK, 2019: Against RCB on April 21, needing 26 off the final over, Dhoni hit 24 runs off the first 5 deliveries, including 3 sixes. Eventually, CSK lost by 1 run as Shardul Thakur was run out, but Dhoni’s 84* is widely considered his best IPL effort.SILENCING CRITICS, 2021: In Qualifier 1 against DC in Dubai, Dhoni scored 18* off 6, smashing 3 consecutive fours in the final over to take CSK home with 2 balls remaining. In the final, they beat KKR to win their 4th title.FIFTH TITLE, 2023: In a rainaffected final against GT, with CSK needing 10 off the last 2 balls, Ravindra Jadeja struck a six and four to seal a 5-wkt win. Dhoni rushed onto the field to embrace Jadeja, later terming it one of the finest moments of his career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test | 'Three pacers, one bowling all-rounder': Tom Latham reveals New Zealand's plan against India
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Tom Latham on Wednesday confirmed that his team will play three fast bowlers and a bowling all-rounder in the two-Test series against
articles.body: New Zealand captain Tom Latham on Wednesday confirmed that his team will play three fast bowlers and a bowling all-rounder in the two-Test series against India. He also made it clear that his side is not focusing on the World Test Championship (WTC) points table.New Zealand are currently at the top of the WTC table with four wins and one loss from six Tests in the current cycle. India are fourth and need to win the series to remain in the race for next year's final."We will play three fast bowlers and one bowling all-rounder," Latham said on the eve of the first Test.The pace attack is expected to feature Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson, along with another fast bowler. The bowling all-rounder will provide an additional option to the attack.'World Test Championship table isn't my focus'New Zealand are currently leading the WTC standings, while India are under pressure to collect points and stay in contention for the final.However, Latham said his team would not get distracted by the points table. He wants his players to focus on their own game and do what they can control."World Test Championship table isn't my focus. We will control the controllables. We will play our brand of cricket and give ourselves the best chance," he said.Latham backs fit-again Matt HenryLatham was happy to have Henry available for the Test series. The experienced pacer is ready to return to red-ball cricket after recovering from a concussion suffered during the ODI series, which New Zealand lost 1-3."Matt Henry is fit and I am hoping he will be excited to perform with the red ball," he said.Jamieson has also impressed the captain with his recent efforts. The fast bowler has been working hard over the past few weeks and has also played in the white-ball matches."Kyle Jamieson bowled well in white ball games and has worked hard in last couple of weeks. He has put in a lot of effort," Latham said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cues from Wellington nets: Shubman Gill, Morne Morkel and '20 good balls'
articles.summary: Wellington: \"20 good balls, yeah?\" was Shubman Gill's polite request to Morne Morkel as the duo prepared for an intriguing contest.
articles.body: Wellington: "20 good balls, yeah?" was Shubman Gill's polite request to Morne Morkel as the duo prepared for an intriguing contest. The practice pitch with the thickest grass cover was the centre of attention as Morkel stood at the top of his mark, some three yards inside the crease. With a mitt in hand, Morkel began firing throwdowns at Gill, who wasn't amused by the ball being hidden inside the oversized glove."Why is the ball in the mitt? Bowlers don't have a mitt," Gill remarked, prompting Morkel to chuckle. "Aah, for the reverse swing," the bowling coach replied.The Indian captain tapped the spot around a good length and asked Morkel to bowl there with a semi-old ball and a scrambled seam. The bowling coach put the right-hander's defence to the test, finding his edge on two occasions and even beating him through the gate with a delivery that came in with the angle. A mini-celebration followed as the lanky fast bowler looked skywards before asking if the moment had been recorded.Gill, meanwhile, got back to business and adopted a tighter approach against the deliveries that followed.He tweaked his trigger movement ever so slightly and looked much more assured after the early wobble. Throwdown specialist Dayanand Garani continued to angle deliveries into the right-hander's pads, but Gill wasn't pleased with those lines. He asked Garani to bowl in a better channel and target the areas where he could challenge his defence. He even explained why the existing line wasn't troubling him enough.The exercise continued for close to 30 minutes before Gill called out, "Final two", wrapping up what was a productive batting workout ahead of the series opener at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. A thick covering of grass, notorious winds and challenging conditions await Gill and Co. from November 19. India have plenty of batting experience in their ranks, but come Thursday, the challenge will be to translate the lessons from the nets into performance against a potent bowling attack.India endured a forgettable batting series the last time they toured these shores. If they are to return with a favourable result this time, much will depend on how their batters adapt to the conditions. The visitors have enough talent and X-factor in their ranks, but the series will be finely poised only if they can put enough runs on the board for their bowlers to work with.India's batting came good during their last away tour of England in 2025, and Gill will hope to replicate his prolific run from that memorable summer. For now, the focus is on getting through those 20 good balls, one delivery at a time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Afghanistan's 20-year-old Naseer Khan Maroofkhil achieves rare Test double last seen in 1965
articles.summary: Afghanistan's 20-year-old all-rounder Naseer Khan Maroofkhil produced a remarkable performance on his Test debut against Zimbabwe in Sharjah, entering the
articles.body: Afghanistan's 20-year-old all-rounder Naseer Khan Maroofkhil produced a remarkable performance on his Test debut against Zimbabwe in Sharjah, entering the record books with a rare double.In the 149-year history of Test cricket, Maroofkhil became only the second player to score a century and take a five-wicket haul in the same match on debut. He also became the youngest player to achieve this feat, at the age of 20 years and 287 days.His performance was special with both bat and ball. Maroofkhil scored 20 runs off 74 balls in the first innings before making an unbeaten 101 off 242 balls in the second.With the ball, he picked up seven wickets for 151 runs in 44 overs in the first innings. He followed it up with two wickets for 106 runs in 37 overs in the second innings.First player to face 300-plus balls and bowl 80-plus overs on debutMaroofkhil also created another record through his workload in the match. e faced a total of 316 balls across his two innings and bowled 81 overs, delivering 486 balls. He became the first player in Test history to face more than 300 deliveries and bowl more than 300 deliveries on his debut.He also became the first player to bat for more than 50 overs and bowl more than 50 overs in a Test debut.Only Bruce Taylor had achieved this double beforeBefore Maroofkhil, only New Zealand's Bruce Taylor had scored a century and taken a five-wicket haul on his Test debut.Taylor achieved the feat against India at Eden Gardens in Kolkata in March 1965. Batting at No. 8, he scored 105 runs in the first innings. He then took five wickets for 86 runs in 23.5 overs in India's first innings.The match ended in a draw. Taylor scored an unbeaten zero in his second innings.Maroofkhil and Taylor remain the only two players to score a century and take five wickets in an innings on their Test debut.Maroofkhil joins elite list of debutantsMaroofkhil also became one of only two players to score at least 100 runs and take eight or more wickets on Test debut. The other player was Albert Trott, who scored 110 runs and took eight wickets against England in Adelaide in 1895.Players with 100+ runs and 8+ wickets on Test debutPlayerOpponentVenueYearRunsWicketsAlbert TrottEnglandAdelaide18951108Nasser Khan MaroofkhilZimbabweSharjah20261219Maroofkhil finished his debut match with 121 runs and nine wickets against Zimbabwe. He also became the third Afghanistan player to score a century on Test debut. Rahmanullah had scored 113 against Zimbabwe in the first Test of the series earlier this month, while Ismat Alam made 101 against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo in January 2025.Maroofkhil's unbeaten 101 is the second-highest individual score by an Afghanistan batter on Test debut, behind Rahmanullah's 113.Fourth Afghan to take a five-wicket haul on debutMaroofkhil is also the fourth Afghanistan bowler to take a five-wicket haul on Test debut. His figures of seven wickets for 151 runs in the first innings are the second-best by an Afghanistan bowler on debut. Ziaur Rahman holds the record with seven wickets for 97 runs in the first innings of his maiden Test.Nasser Khan Maroofkhil's performance on Test debutInningsBattingBowlingFirst innings20 (74 balls)7/151 (44 overs)Second innings101* (242 balls)2/106 (37 overs)Total121 runs9 wicketsGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Beyond being Mohammad Nabi's son: Hassan Eisakhil's wants to make his own mark
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Being the son of a legendary cricketer comes with its own set of expectations, and Hassan Eisakhil is beginning to understand the weight of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Being the son of a legendary cricketer comes with its own set of expectations, and Hassan Eisakhil is beginning to understand the weight of that legacy. The 20-year-old is the son of Mohammad Nabi, one of the pioneers of Afghanistan cricket, who, at 41, continues to defy age and remains an integral part of the senior national team. Nabi has also expressed his desire to share the dressing room with his son in Afghan colours one day.Eisakhil, however, is unfazed by the expectations that come with being Mohammad Nabi's son. For now, the young opener is focused on developing his game and making a name for himself.He is very strict during training and practice. After that, we are like friends and talk normally. So, I would say he is strict during training."So far, I haven't felt any pressure about being Mohammad Nabi's son. I just play my natural game. Whatever I have learnt from playing cricket, I try to put into practice. I don't do anything extra," Eisakhil told TimesofIndia.com in an interview facilitated by Sony Sports Network ahead of the Asia Cup Rising Stars, which begins on Thursday in Doha, Qatar."We talk about cricket a lot at home. I ask him questions, and he shares his experiences with me. He also points out my mistakes and watches our matches. He helps me a lot," he said.Eisakhil breaks into a smile when asked whether his father is a hard taskmaster."He is very strict during training and practice. After that, we are like friends and talk normally. So, I would say he is strict during training," he said.Inshallah, we will play together in the national jersey as well. It depends on how I perform. If I perform really well, I will make it to the national team.The father-son duo recently played together in the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL), and Eisakhil hopes that one day fans will see them represent Afghanistan together in the national jersey. It is a "dream" that Nabi expressed in 2025. The son echoes that now."Inshallah, we will play together in the national jersey as well. It depends on how I perform. If I perform really well, I will make it to the national team," Eisakhil said.Afghanistan open their campaign against Sri Lanka A on Thursday, and the young opener, who has already represented his country at the Under-19 level, is eager to make the most of the opportunity."The preparation is going well. Recently, we haven't played many ODIs, as we have been involved in a lot of T20 tournaments. So, we had a camp in Jalalabad, where we held a few practice sessions and played some intra-squad ODI matches. The preparation has been good," Eisakhil said.Ever since I started playing cricket in 2020, I have watched Virat Kohli play. I admire his passion for the game, his fitness levels, the way he bats and how he calculates a chase.Eisakhil shares some batting similarities with his father, but unlike Nabi, he is a top-order batter. Having already played a couple of T20Is for Afghanistan at the Asian Games, he is aware that breaking into the senior team's established opening combination of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran will not be easy."The competition is very strong, but I take it as motivation to work harder. Inshallah, I will make it to the national team through my performances soon," he said.Despite being the son of one of Afghanistan's cricketing greats, Eisakhil looks up to two Indian batting stars: Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill."I would say Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli. I admire the way they maintain discipline and consistency in their work," he said."Ever since I started playing cricket in 2020, I have watched Virat Kohli play. I admire his passion for the game, his fitness levels, the way he bats and how he calculates a chase. The way he approaches and chases any target is something I really love," he added.As a top-order batter, Eisakhil is keen to incorporate some of Kohli's methods into his own game, particularly when chasing targets."I am working on that. I am trying to understand how to pace an innings and handle pressure situations. I work on these aspects with my father and Afghanistan's domestic coaches. I also ask them questions, and I am gradually getting a better understanding of the game."For now, Eisakhil is not looking too far ahead. The prospect of playing alongside his father in Afghanistan colours remains a dream, but he knows that the journey towards it will have to be built on his own performances. With Nabi's experience to draw upon and the likes of Kohli and Gill to inspire him, the 20-year-old is keen to carve out an identity of his own.*Watch ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026, starting November 19, Thursday from 11:30 AM IST LIVE and Exclusive on Sony Sports Network channels and Sony LIV.*Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi needs right set of people around him: Dinesh Karthik
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Indian cricket's wonderkid 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is \"ruling the world,\" but \"needs a good support system, the right set of people
articles.body: MUMBAI: Indian cricket's wonderkid 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is "ruling the world," but "needs a good support system, the right set of people around him, the coaches, the family," feels former India wicketkeeper Dinesh Karthik, currently IPL defending champions’ Royal Challengers Bengaluru’s batting coach and mentor."For the longest time, probably for the last half a decade maybe, that I've been part of the job. There's not an event that I've gone to where they have not asked me about Kohli or Rohit. The new one to enter the list is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Wherever I go these days, there's a question about him. It's very interesting, isn't it? At the age of 14, I was trying to understand how to finish my maths homework and here is a kid who is ruling the world right now. But in him lies the challenge. And when I say challenge, I'm talking about society in general. And that includes people like me who hold on to a microphone and have views about him. I think it's important for a lot of precocious talent to also fall and land sometimes, understand from mistakes and have acceptance from our side. He needs what I call a really good support system, the right set of people around him, the coaches, the family. The most important people being the public who view him and people like me who are broadcasting and have a view on him," Karthik said at an Sustainable Markets Initiative event, organised by the prestigious Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) and the Mumbai Cricket Association, at the MCA Lounge in the Wankhede Stadium on Tuesday.Comparing Sooryavanshi to a young Sachin Tendulkar, Karthik said, "To understand that he's 14-years-old, understand the nature of the beast which is this game which is right now at its strongest financially in terms of the amount of people who are following this game and the different formats and the challenges that go along with it. He's a kid. And he's extraordinarily talented. You don't get that kind of talent. I think the last person who's probably as spoken about and viewed as in terms of talent is from this city, Sachin Tendulkar. So, he became the greatest ever to have played this game. As you know, we literally refer to him as the god of cricket. That's how much we regularly look up to him and what he's achieved is something that we all look up to as standard and at times unachievable. I do feel Sooryavanshi is that kind of a talent. And for him, I'd say, have a smile. Enjoy the journey."Karthik urged the fans and critics to "allow him to grow as a cricketer." "And for the rest of us, I'd say, watch what you say about him. Allow him to grow and learn as a cricketer. Because the pressures of today are very different to what it was two decades ago. I genuinely wish him the best of luck. He's an extraordinary talent. And you can't stop such a talent at the age of 14. He's that good that he's forcing his way into playing in the T20 format, which is probably one of the toughest to get into. But that's how talented he is. You don't want to stop a talent like that. But you want to make sure that the support staff around him is very strong.Unlike an emerging Tendulkar from three decades ago, Sooryavanshi has the endure the added pressure of a relentless social media. Reiterating his point about the importance of having the right kind of advisors around Sooryanbshi who would help him make the right choices in life, Karthik said, "That's the world we live in today. I know there's plenty of offers for him on the table to do various things off the field. And that's where he needs a good set of heads helping him and choosing the right position. And for the modern-day cricketer, I think there are a lot of good things about social media. But there are also a lot of things. If you don't have discipline, and you don't have the right set of eyes, you could get into the wrong sort of lane, if I could say that. So, as much as you would want to explore and become the best cricketer, you need to know where you want to draw the line. And your relationship with social media, and in general the media, is very important."Karthik advised Sooryavanshi and other young cricketers to "filter out what's important and leave out the rest." "There is no doubt that today's cricketers are under a lot more scrutiny. Because every person, even before, had a view, but they had no place to express it. But today, because of social media, every person can put their view outside. If you start looking at every opinion about you, I feel like it becomes a very hard place to live. You need to be able to kind of filter out what's important and leave out the rest," Karthik said.Meanwhile, Karthik revealed that RCB felt the pressure of defending the IPL title in 2026 much more than winning it for the first time in 2025. “The pressure of trying to defend something, hold on to something is completely alien to RCB at that stage, and to defend a title was a lot more challenging.
